But for those who would not believe it without such authorities, let them rub their mouths thoroughly with a couple of chilies and see if they find them cooling. Thus, when certain teachers among these great healers <note>The original term *ensalmaderas* refers to women who healed through a mix of folk medicine and chanted prayers or "charms."</note> or herbalists say that the chili is "cool," and other times that it is "moist," instead of giving them credit, we shall laugh at their folly. For in what they say, they make neither head nor tail <note>original: "no atan ni desatan," an idiom meaning their words lack logic or impact.</note>; because if credit is to be given to the reasoning and judgment of Galen <note>Galen of Pergamon (129–216 AD) was the most influential physician in the Western tradition; his theories on the four "humors" dominated medicine for 1,500 years.</note>, the chili is of greater heat than black pepper. And so we see that it scorches the vitals and wounds the intestines, and even tends to cause bloody stools <note>original: "camaras de sangre," a historical term for dysentery or severe intestinal inflammation.</note> and inflammations of the liver, doing no less than a most burning poison. Supposing then that the chili is so extremely hot, I say secondly: that if this chili is toasted, it loses much of its heat, and the same happens with pepper and every sharp and biting <term>mordicative</term> <note>something that causes a stinging or biting sensation on the skin or tongue</note> thing. The cause of this is now sought: because if one looks closely, it should rather have gained heat from the fire; for even Galen, speaking of salt and other things brought near the fire, says himself that they gain greater heat from the fire.

The response to this is to say plainly that the chili, the pepper, and everything that bites is very "hot," and likewise loses that heat with fire. The cause is that such heat was not fixed and deposited throughout the entire object, but rather in certain subtle and very delicate parts. Since the fire wasted and consumed these, the toasted item remained without its heat. I will give an example: the onion and the garlic, before they were cooked, were sharp and gave much heat; after being cooked, they neither bite nor provide heat. The cause is that the heat of the fire consumed those most subtle parts which were what gave heat to the onion. Thus, with these lost and wasted, the onion lacks them and remains "cool." This same thing happens to the chili with fire, being (as I have said) composed of most subtle and very hot parts. However, a "cold" thing, or one composed of thick <note>In Galenic science, "thick" or "gross" parts refer to the dense, earthy matter of a substance, as opposed to its "subtle" or volatile essences.</note> parts, will not experience this; for it lacks the hot and subtle parts for the fire to waste, but rather the fire will thin the thick parts it does have and leave heat within them.

The same poet calls them <term>diotrepheas basilēas</term> <gloss>Zeus-nurtured kings</gloss>, kings educated by <term>Jupiter</term>. Furthermore, the silent voice of nature is that monarchy is to be preferred. One king for bees, one for elephants, one ruler in the herd; cranes follow one leader; the one <term>Sun</term> presides over the day, the one <term>Moon</term> over the night, which is like the queen of the starry lights. In a ship there is one pilot, in a house one paterfamilias, in an army the sign of one. In the limbs the heart moves all things: in the parts of the soul reason presides: in the universe the one <term>God</term> is the creator and ruler of all. Although these things are most known, even to the bleary-eyed and the barbers <note>a classical proverb meaning things known to everyone</note>; yet there are those who both extol the mob and stir up mobs: there are those who prefer to be vexed by many than by one: there are, finally, those who admire, venerate, and embrace the womanly rule of a man. Not worthy of the name of men. I would wish that they also offered a fan and made a breeze. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, saying: The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles <term>Sukkot</term> <gloss>Booths/Tabernacles</gloss> for seven days to the Lord. On the first day shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no servile work therein. Seven days you shall offer an offering made by fire to the Lord. On the eighth day shall be a holy convocation to you; and you shall offer an offering made by fire to the Lord; it is a solemn assembly; and you shall do no servile work therein. These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, to offer an offering made by fire to the Lord, a burnt offering, and a meal offering, a sacrifice, and drink offerings, everything upon its day; beside the sabbaths of the Lord, and beside your gifts, and beside all your vows, and beside all your freewill offerings, which you give to the Lord. Also in the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the fruit of the land, you shall keep a feast to the Lord seven days; on the first day shall be a sabbath, and on the eighth day shall be a sabbath. And you shall take you on the first day the fruit of goodly trees <note>traditionally interpreted as the etrog (citron)</note>, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook; and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days. And you shall keep it a feast to the Lord seven days in the year. It shall be a statute forever in your generations; you shall celebrate it in the seventh month. You shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are home-born in Israel shall dwell in booths.

<column-break/>

...that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God. And Moses declared to the children of Israel the feasts of the Lord.

->[OF THE] CELESTIAL HIERARCHY<-
<note>original: "οὐρανίας ἱεραρχίας." This is the running header of the book.</note>

->[c ii]<-
<note>This is a "signature mark," used by early printers to keep the pages in the correct order for binding.</note>

...deeming [our hierarchy] worthy of a **super-worldly** <note>literally "hyper-cosmic," meaning existing beyond the physical universe</note> imitation of the celestial hierarchies. By diversifying the immaterial hierarchies with material shapes and formal compositions, Scripture has handed them down to us. This was done so that, in a way proportionate to our own nature, we might be led upward from these most sacred fashioned-forms to the simple, formless elevations and likenesses. 

For it is not possible for our human mind to be extended toward that immaterial imitation and contemplation of the celestial hierarchies unless it uses the **material guidance** <note>"hylaia cheiragogia," literally "material hand-holding." A key concept in Dionysius where physical objects "lead us by the hand" to God</note> suited to it. It must consider visible beauties as icons of invisible loveliness, and sensory fragrances as imprints of the **intellectual distribution** <note>original: "noētēs diadosis" — the way God "spreads" or "distributes" his presence into the mind</note> of God. 

It must see material lights as an image of the immaterial gift of light, and the detailed sacred teachings of the priests as a reflection of the mind's own contemplative fulfillment. We should view the orderly arrangements of our ceremonies here on earth as a way to reach a harmonious and ordered habit toward divine things. Furthermore, we should see the participation in the most divine **Eucharist** <note>literally "thanksgiving," referring to the central Christian rite of communion</note> as a way of sharing in the fellowship of Jesus. In short, all those things that are given to the celestial beings in a **super-worldly** manner are handed down to us through symbols.

<margin>T</margin>herefore, for the sake of this proportionate **deification** <note>"theosis." The process of becoming "god-like" or united with God through grace</note> of ours, the benevolent **Source of Rites** <note>"Teletarchia." A title for God or Christ as the one who initiates and perfects all sacred ceremonies</note> has revealed the celestial hierarchies to us. By making our own earthly hierarchy a "fellow-minister" with them through this likeness—as far as our power allows—the Source has described the super-celestial beings through sensory images in the holy scriptures.

### VOCABULARY
*   **Celestial hierarchies**: The ordered ranks of angels in heaven.
*   **Imitation**: The process by which a lower rank tries to mirror the qualities of a higher rank.
*   **Immaterial things**: Realities that have no physical body or "matter."
*   **Intellectual distribution**: The way spiritual truths are shared or spread into the human intellect.
*   **Most divine Eucharist**: The sacrament of the Lord's Supper, viewed here as a way for humans to participate in the life of Jesus.
*   **Source of Rites**: The divine principle that establishes and governs all sacred rituals.
*   **Deification**: The ultimate goal of the soul, which is to be made like God.

<summary>Dionysius explains that material symbols—like light, fragrance, and the Eucharist—are necessary tools that "lead the human mind by the hand" toward immaterial spiritual truths. He argues that the earthly church hierarchy is a symbolic mirror of the angelic hierarchy in heaven, designed to help humans achieve deification.</summary>

**Chapter XXVI. On the rational acts of certain animals.**

Consider the acts of certain animals that seem to show the inspiration of reason. Among a thousand examples, take these best-known ones: the government of bees, the foresight of ants, and the skill of the spider in spreading its nets. Are these the work of a reason belonging to these animals themselves? If so, this reason would be either superior, inferior, or equal to that of man. But if these animals had a reason more enlightened than ours, they would act better than man in all or nearly all circumstances; and it is plain that most of the time they fall short of him. If this reason were inferior, each of them would not devote itself exclusively to a single work and bring it almost to perfection; for it seems to be the mark of an accomplished intelligence, superior to man's, always to apply itself to a single work so as to make it as perfect as possible. Finally, if their mind were equal to man's, it would not concentrate in this way on a single task, only to show itself inferior to human works in everything else. For reports explicitly state that the disobedient will be punished, as in God Almighty's words: "There is none of you but will pass through it" <note>Qur'an 19:71</note>, which is unequivocal that this must occur for everyone, since no believer is free from committing a sin. And as for His words: "None shall burn therein except the most wretched" <note>Qur'an 92:15</note>, He meant a specific group thereby, just as He intended a specific individual by "the most wretched." And His words: "Every time a group is cast into it" <note>Qur'an 67:8</note> means a group from among the disbelievers. The contextual restriction of such general expressions is straightforward, unlike interpretations that reduce speech to poetic hyperbole.

A group among the speculative theologians denied the very validity of general forms of speech, holding that these verses must be suspended until some accompanying contextual indicator clarifies their meaning. As for the <term>Mu'tazilites</term> <gloss>an early rationalist theological school that asserted the absolute necessity of punishment for unrepentant grave sinners</gloss>, their doubt rests on God Almighty's words: "And indeed, I am most forgiving toward him who repents, believes, and works righteousness" <note>Qur'an 20:82</note>; and His words: "By the declining day, indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds" <note>Qur'an 103:1-3</note>; and His words: "There is none of you but will pass through it," followed immediately by: "Then We will save those who feared God" <note>Qur'an 19:71-72</note>; and His words: "And whoever disobeys God and His messenger, then indeed for him is the fire of Hell" <note>Qur'an 72:23</note>. Thus His speech explicitly conjoins righteous action with faith. They also point to His words: "And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell" <note>Qur'an 4:93</note>.

Yet these general texts are likewise restricted, by virtue of the evidence in His words: "And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills" <note>Qur'an 4:48</note>. It is necessary, therefore, to affirm for Him a divine will in the forgiveness of sins other than <term>shirk</term> <gloss>polytheism or attributing partners to God</gloss>. In the same way, there is the tradition: "Whoever has in his heart even the weight of a speck of dust of faith shall be brought out of the Fire"; and His words: "Indeed, God does not cause the reward of those who do good to be lost" <note>Qur'an 9:120</note>.
